gloss: A jointed or flexible device that allows the pivoting of a door etc.
A wall-mounted socket connected to an electrical power supply, at which current can be taken to run electrical devices.
example: I had to move the cupboard to get to the power outlet.

gloss: A hard white translucent ceramic, originally made by firing kaolin, quartz, and feldspar at high temperatures but now also inclusive of similar artificial materials; also often (figurative) such a material as a symbol of the fragility, elegance, etc. traditionally associated with porcelain goods.
example: Tableware and toilets are both made of porcelain.

gloss: Synonym of porcelain, a hard white translucent ceramic made from kaolin, now (chiefly US) sometimes distinguished in reference to tableware as fine or good china.
example: It's a china doll.

gloss: A flat, rigid structure, fixed at right angles to a wall or forming a part of a cabinet, desk, etc., and used to display, store, or support objects.
example: We keep the old newspapers on the bottom shelf of the cupboard, and our photos on the top shelf.

gloss: An open-topped box that can be slid in and out of the cabinet that contains it, used for storing clothing or other articles.
A cabinet, closet, or other piece of furniture with shelves intended for storing cookware, dishware, or food; similar cabinets or closets used for storing other items.
example: Put the cups back into the cupboard.

gloss: A movable cupboard or cabinet designed for storing clothes, particularly as a large piece of bedroom furniture.
The overhead closure of a room.
example: The dining room had an ornate ceiling.

gloss: The interior bottom or surface of a house or building; the supporting surface of a room.
example: The room has a wooden floor.

gloss: A piece of cloth covering a window, bed, etc. to offer privacy and keep out light.
example: He drew the curtains at 11:00pm before falling asleep.

gloss: A fabric used as a complete floor covering.
A partial covering for a floor.
A soft mass of material stuffed into a cloth bag, used for comfort or support.
A soft cushion used to support the head in bed.
A heavy, loosely woven fabric, usually large and woollen, used for warmth while sleeping or resting.
example: The baby was cold, so his mother put a blanket over him.

gloss: A quilt or usually flat cloth bag with a filling (traditionally down) and usually an additional washable cover, used instead of blankets; often called a comforter or quilt, especially in US English.
example: He pulled the thick duvet over his head to block out the morning light.

gloss: A pad on which a person can recline and sleep, usually having an inner section of coiled springs covered with foam or other cushioning material then enclosed with cloth fabric.
A washable, easily removable cloth cover for pillows.
A cloth used for wiping, especially one used for drying anything wet, such as a person after a bath.
example: He needed a towel for wiping the slippery floor.

gloss: An exposed plumbing fitting; a tap or spigot; a regulator for controlling the flow of a liquid from a reservoir.
example: The rain ceased as if a faucet had been turned off.

gloss: A basin used for holding water for washing.
A large container for holding water in which a person may bathe (take a bath).
example: I had a long, leisurely soak in the bathtub.

gloss: A device for bathing by which water is made to fall on the body from a height, either from a tank or by the action of a pump.
A conduit allowing liquid to flow out of an otherwise contained volume; a plughole (UK)
example: The drain in the kitchen sink is clogged.

gloss: A smooth surface, usually made of glass with reflective material painted on the underside, that reflects light so as to give an image of what is in front of it.
example: I had a look in the mirror to see if the blood had come off my face.

gloss: A coarse mat at the entrance to a house, upon which one wipes one's shoes.
example: Wipe your shoes on the doormat before you start plodding around in the house.

gloss: A bell, buzzer, or chime device mounted on or adjacent to a door's exterior, meant to be rung by a visitor to announce one's presence.
The lowermost part of a doorway that one crosses to enter; a sill.
example: Near-synonym: doorstep

gloss: A flight of stairs; a stairway.
A fence or barrier consisting of one or more horizontal rails and vertical supports.
example: During the war, everyone's railings were taken away to make bombers.

gloss: The space, often unfinished and with sloped walls, directly below the roof in the uppermost part of a house or other building, generally used for storage or habitation.
example: We went up to the attic to look for the boxes containing our childhood keepsakes.

gloss: A floor of a building below ground level.
An accessible structure extending from a building, especially outside a window.
A vertical tube or hollow column used to emit environmentally polluting gaseous and solid matter (including but not limited to by-products of burning carbon- or hydrocarbon-based fuels); a flue.
An open hearth for holding a fire at the base of a chimney.
A finned metal fixture that carries hot water or steam in order to heat a room.
example: The radiator kept the apartment warm during winter.

gloss: A device that automatically responds to changes in temperature by activating a heating or cooling system to maintain the temperature at a desired setting.
A device that uses suction, and often agitation, in order to remove dirt and other debris from carpets and hard floors.
A domestic utensil with fibers bound together at the end of a long handle, used for sweeping.
example: Meronyms: broomstick (handle), bavin (head)

gloss: A flat scoop with a handle, into which dust, dirt and other material is conveyed with a brush or broom.
An implement for washing floors or similar, made of a piece of cloth, or a collection of thrums, or coarse yarn, fastened to a handle.
Any non-soap cleaning agent, especially a synthetic surfactant.
example: Near-synonym: cleaner (sometimes coordinate)

gloss: A place or room where laundering is done - including, by extension, other forms of laundering than clothes washing.
A clip or fastener used to secure garments to a clothesline while drying, and sometimes for other applications requiring holding or pinching.
Large movable item(s), usually in a room, which enhance(s) the room's characteristics, functionally or decoratively.
example: The woman does not even have one stick of furniture moved in yet.

gloss: A person that leases real property; a lessor.
One who holds a lease (a tenancy).
A payment made by a tenant at intervals in order to lease a property.
example: I am asking £300 a week rent.

gloss: A (usually) metal fastener consisting of a partially or completely threaded shank, sometimes with a threaded point, and a head used to both hold the top material and to drive the screw either directly into a soft material or into a prepared hole.
A hand tool or power tool which engages with the head of a screw and allows torque to be applied to turn the screw, thus driving it in or loosening it.

A spike-shaped metal fastener used for joining wood or similar materials. The nail is generally driven through two or more layers of material by means of impacts from a hammer or other device. It is then held in place by friction.
example: Yesterday my shirt got torn after I caught it on a nail.

gloss: A tool with a heavy head and a handle used for pounding.
example: Bobby used a hammer and nails to fix the two planks together.

gloss: A pincer-like gripping tool that multiplies the strength of the user's hand, often used for bending things.
example: I need a pair of pliers to get a good grip on that broken screw.

gloss: A hand tool for making rotational adjustments, such as fitting nuts and bolts, or fitting pipes.
A tool or machine used to remove material so as to create a hole, typically by plunging a rotating cutting bit into a stationary workpiece.
example: Wear safety glasses when operating an electric drill.

gloss: Such a tool with a toothed blade.
example: Meronyms: sawtooth < sawblade

gloss: A frame, usually portable, of wood, metal, or rope, used for ascent and descent, consisting of two side pieces to which are fastened rungs (cross strips or rounds acting as steps).
A graduated flexible ribbon used for measuring lengths.
A tool employing a chamber with a colored liquid (usually alcohol, hence spirit) and an air bubble, used to determine a horizontal or vertical reference line.
Strong paper coated with (traditionally) sand or (today) manufactured aluminum oxide, silicon carbide, or other abrasive material, used for smoothing and polishing.
example: Near-synonym: emery paper

gloss: A thin brush for applying paint.
A cylindrical tool for applying paint or ink.
A clear or translucent liquid coating composed of resin dissolved in a solvent, which dries by evaporation to form a hard, protective, and typically glossy finish.
A hard gelatin made by boiling bones and hides, used in solution as an adhesive; or any sticky adhesive substance.
example: Near-synonyms: adhesive, cement

gloss: Tape with an adhesive film on one side, used to attach materials to something.

A (usually) metal fastener consisting of a cylindrical body that is threaded, with a larger head on one end. It can be inserted into an unthreaded hole up to the head, with a nut then threaded on the other end; a heavy machine screw.

A piece of hardware, typically metal and typically hexagonal or square in shape, with a hole through it having internal screw threads, intended to be screwed onto a threaded bolt or other threaded shaft.

A flat piece of material, often of metal and often an annulus, placed beneath a nut or at some joint, to distribute pressure, alleviate friction, provide directionally differentiated friction (e.g. making the nut turn counter-clockwise only with difficulty), or prevent leakage.
Metal formed into a thin, even thread, now usually by being drawn through a hole in a steel die.
example: Holonyms: cable; wire rope; wiring harness; wire wool

gloss: An assembly of two or more wires, used for electrical power or data circuits; one or more and/or the whole may be insulated.
A pronged connecting device which fits into a mating socket, especially an electrical one.
example: I pushed the plug back into the electrical socket and the lamp began to glow again.

gloss: A device to prevent excessive overcurrent from overload or short circuit in an electrical circuit, containing a component that melts and interrupts the current when too high a load is passed through it.
A rigid tube that transports water, steam, or other fluid, as used in plumbing and numerous other applications.
A crack, crevice, fissure, or hole which admits water or other fluid, or lets it escape.
example: a leak in a roof

gloss: A tight closure, secure against leakage.
example: Close the lid tightly to get a good seal.

gloss: The deteriorated state of iron or steel as a result of moisture and oxidation; it consists mostly of iron(III) oxide (ferric oxide) and iron(II) oxide (ferrous oxide).
example: The rust on my bicycle chain made cycling to work very dangerous.

gloss: A disruption, mark or shallow cut on a surface made by scratching.
example: I can’t believe there is a scratch in the paint already.

gloss: A shallow deformation in the surface of an object, produced by an impact.
example: The crash produced a dent in the left side of the car.

gloss: The sharp sound made when solid material breaks.
example: The crack of the falling branch could be heard for miles.

gloss: The substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree. Used as a material for construction, to manufacture various items, etc. or as fuel.
example: This table is made of wood.

gloss: Construction material supplied in sheets, and made of three or more layers of wood veneer glued together, laid up with alternating layers having their grain perpendicular to each other.
example: After the hurricane there was a severe regional shortage of plywood, especially exterior plywood.

gloss: An artificial metal produced from iron, harder and more elastic than elemental iron; used figuratively as a symbol of hardness.
A reddish-brown metallic chemical element (symbol Cu) with the atomic number 29; also, the metal made up of this element.
A building material created by mixing cement, water, and aggregate such as gravel and sand.
example: Various types of concrete have been used in the construction of this highway.

gloss: A hardened rectangular block of mud, clay etc., used for building.
example: This wall is made of bricks.

gloss: A regularly-shaped slab of clay or other material, affixed to cover or decorate a surface, as in a roof-tile, glazed tile, stove tile, carpet tile, etc.
To make tighter.
example: Please tighten that screw a quarter-turn.

gloss: To make loose.
example: to loosen a knot; to loosen one's grip / hold on something

gloss: To supply or substitute an equivalent with.
example: I replaced my car with a newer model.

gloss: To restore to good working order, fix, or improve damaged condition; to mend; to remedy.
example: to repair a house, a road, a shoe, a ship

gloss: To put together.
example: He assembled the model ship.

gloss: To ascertain the quantity of a unit of material via calculated comparison with respect to a standard.
example: We measured the temperature with a thermometer.

gloss: To connect, set up or prepare something for use
To disconnect from a supply, especially an electrical socket.
example: To save electricity, I unplug my computer when I am not at home.

gloss: Any of a variety of materials designed to reduce the flow of heat, either from or into a building.
An opening into which a plug or other connecting part is designed to fit (e.g. a light bulb socket).
example: Near-synonyms: jack, outlet, receptacle, wall socket

gloss: Any of various large coniferous evergreen trees or shrubs from the genus Picea, found in northern temperate and boreal regions; originally and more fully spruce fir.
Any coniferous tree of the genus Pinus.
example: The northern slopes were covered mainly in pine.

gloss: A deciduous tree with distinctive deeply lobed leaves, acorns, and notably strong wood, typically of England and northeastern North America, included in genus Quercus.
A tree of the genus Fagus having a smooth, light grey trunk, oval, pointed leaves, and many branches.
Any of various trees of the genus Betula, native to countries in the Northern Hemisphere.
Any of various deciduous trees or shrubs in the genus Salix, in the willow family Salicaceae, found primarily on moist soils in cooler zones in the northern hemisphere.

A small tree (Acer campestre), known as the common maple, field maple, or hedge maple, which has palmate leaves with five lobes and winged seeds, and is chiefly native to East Asia, Europe, North Africa, and North America.

An edible nut (technically a fruit) of the Spanish chestnut or sweet chestnut tree (Castanea sativa); also (chiefly preceded by a descriptive word), a nut from a related shrub or tree; or a similar nut from an unrelated plant.
A shade tree of the genus Fraxinus.
example: The ash trees are dying off due to emerald ash borer.

gloss: A conifer of the genus Abies.
The usually single, more or less upright part of a tree, between the roots and the branches.
The exterior covering of the trunk and branches of a tree or of various other woody plants.
The woody part of a tree arising from the trunk and usually dividing.
A small thin branch of a tree or bush.
example: They used twigs and leaves as a base to start the fire.

gloss: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
example: This tree's roots can go as deep as twenty metres underground.

gloss: The usually green and flat organ that represents the most prominent feature of most vegetative plants.
A needle-like leaf found on some conifers.
The fruit of a conifer or a similarly shaped fruit or flower head of certain other plants, such as banksias and proteas.
The fruit of the oak, being an oval nut growing in a woody cup or cupule.
Any alga, lichen, bryophyte, or other plant of seemingly simple structure.
example: Spanish moss

gloss: Any of a group of some twenty thousand species of vascular plants classified in the division Pteridophyta that lack seeds and reproduce by shedding spores to initiate an alternation of generations.
Any of several woody, climbing, or trailing evergreen plants of the genus Hedera.
A thicket of bushes or other shrubbery, especially one planted as a fence between two portions of land, or to separate the parts of a garden.
example: He trims the hedge once a week.

gloss: A woody plant smaller than a tree, and usually with several stems from the same base.
Any plant unwanted at the place where and at the time when it is growing.
example: If it isn't in a straight line or marked with a label, it's a weed.

gloss: Ground (generally in front of or around a house) covered with grass kept closely mown.
A mixture of mineral particles and organic material, used to support plant growth.
example: We bought a bag of soil for the houseplants.

gloss: A small stone, especially one rounded by the action of water.
Small fragments of rock, used for laying on the beds of roads and railways, and as ballast.
A field or pasture; a piece of land either intentionally cultivated with grass or (especially) naturally covered with grass, especially one that is intended to be mown for hay or to be grazed.
example: alpine meadows

gloss: Ground covered with grass or herbage, used or suitable for the grazing of livestock.
A dense uncultivated tract of trees and undergrowth, larger than woods.
An area of land within a wood or forest devoid of trees.
An inland body of standing water, either natural or man-made, that is smaller than a lake.
A small river; a large creek; a body of moving water confined by banks.
A sloped side of a river acting as a barrier between the water and level ground to either side.
Any of the rodents of the family Sciuridae.
example: tree squirrels

gloss: A small mammal of the subfamily Erinaceinae, characterized by their spiny back and often by the habit of rolling up into a ball when attacked, native to Afro-Eurasia.
A ruminant mammal with hooves and often antlers, of the family Cervidae, or one of several similar animals from related families of the order Artiodactyla, such as the musk deer or mouse deer.
Any member of the genus Vulpes; a true fox.
Any member of species of the genera Meles, Arctonyx, Mellivora or Taxidea, of mammals.

Any of various birds of prey of the order Strigiformes, families Strigidae and Tytonidae, that are primarily nocturnal and have forward-looking, binocular vision, limited eye movement, and good hearing.
The house sparrow, Passer domesticus; a small bird with a short bill, and brown, white and gray feathers.
A European robin, Erithacus rubecula.
Any of numerous species of insect in the order Coleoptera characterized by a pair of hard, shell-like front wings which cover and protect a pair of rear wings when at rest.
Any of many types of stinging flying insect resembling a hornet.
The larva of a butterfly or moth; leafworm.
example: The bird just ate that green caterpillar.

gloss: Any of very many animals (either hermaphroditic or nonhermaphroditic), of the class Gastropoda, having a coiled shell.
A worm that lives in the ground.
Any of the several species of plant in the genus Taraxacum, characterised by yellow flower heads and notched, broad-ended leaves, especially the common dandelion (Taraxacum officinale).
Light rain.
A heavy fall of rain.
example: They got caught in a downpour without an umbrella and came back soaked.

gloss: A brief fall of precipitation (spell of rain, or a similar fall of snow, sleet, or cascade); burst of hefty precipitation.
example: Today there will be frequent showers and some sunny spells.

gloss: Balls or pieces of ice falling as precipitation, often in connection with a thunderstorm.
Pellets of ice made of mostly-frozen raindrops or refrozen melted snowflakes.
A cover of minute ice crystals on objects that are exposed to the air. Frost is formed by the same process as dew, except that the temperature of the frosted object is below freezing.
Any moisture from the atmosphere condensed by cool bodies upon their surfaces.
A thick cloud that forms near the ground; the obscurity of such a cloud.
example: a bank of fog

gloss: Water or other liquid finely suspended in air. (Compare fog, haze.)
example: It was difficult to see through the morning mist.

gloss: A light, gentle wind.
example: The breeze rustled the papers on her desk.

gloss: A strong, abrupt rush of wind.
The loud rumbling, cracking, or crashing sound caused by expansion of rapidly heated air around a lightning bolt.
example: Thunder is preceded by lightning.

gloss: A flash of light produced by short-duration, high-voltage discharge of electricity within a cloud, between clouds, or between a cloud and the earth.
example: Although we did not see the lightning, we did hear the thunder.

gloss: A period of unusually low rainfall, longer and more severe than a dry spell.
example: His village had faced a drought twice.

gloss: An overflow of a large amount of water (usually disastrous) from a lake or other body of water due to excessive rainfall or other input of water.
Dampness, especially that of the air.
example: The high humidity made the air feel sticky and hot.

gloss: A prediction of the weather.
example: The forecast said it'll be blowy tomorrow

gloss: Covered with clouds; overshadowed; darkened; (meteorology) more than 90% covered by clouds.
Cold enough to cause discomfort.
Moderately warm, especially less cold than expected.
example: a mild day

gloss: Of a surface, having low friction, often due to being covered in a non-viscous liquid, and therefore hard to grip, hard to stand on without falling, etc.
example: Oily substances render things slippery.

gloss: Covered or splashed with, or full of, mud (“wet soil”).
example: He slogged across the muddy field.

gloss: Of a near-vertical gradient; of a slope, surface, curve, etc. that proceeds upward or downward at an angle approaching vertical.
example: a steep hill or mountain; a steep roof; a steep ascent; a steep barometric gradient

gloss: A surface that either inclines or declines in a regular manner from the perspective of an observer.
example: the slope

gloss: A vertical (or nearly vertical) rock face.
example: , scar

gloss: An elongated depression cast between hills or mountains, often with a river flowing through it.
example: The Indus River valley was the site of an ancient civilization.

gloss: A chain of mountains.
The highest point of a hill, mountain, or similar geographical feature.
example: In summer, it is possible to hike to the summit of Mount Shasta.

gloss: Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
example: lake shore; bay shore; gulf shore; island shore; mainland shore; river shore; estuary shore; pond shore; sandy shore; rocky shore

gloss: The daily fluctuation in the level of the sea caused by the gravitational influence of the moon and the sun.
example: The Bristol Channel has some of the world's largest tides.

gloss: A moving disturbance in the level of a body of liquid; an undulation.
example: The wave traveled from the center of the lake before breaking on the shore.

gloss: The generally unidirectional movement of a gas or fluid.
A body of water (especially the sea) contained by a concave shoreline.
example: This hotel has a great view across the bay.

gloss: A piece of land projecting into water from a larger land mass.
A flow of water over the edge of a cliff.
A route for travel over land, especially a narrow, unpaved pathway for use by hikers, horseback riders, etc.
A small, often temporary, pool of water, usually on a path or road.
The time of day when the sun appears above the eastern horizon.
example: I'll meet you at the docks at sunrise.

gloss: The moment each evening when the sun disappears below the western horizon.
example: at sunset

gloss: The skeletal joint which connects the foot with the leg; the uppermost portion of the foot and lowermost portion of the leg, which contain this skeletal joint.
The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.
example: With a flick of the wrist, he threw the frisbee to a team-mate.

gloss: The joint between the upper arm and the forearm.
The joint between the arm and the torso, sometimes including the surrounding muscles, tendons, and ligaments.
The bottom of a face, (specifically) the typically jutting jawline below the mouth.
example: What does it mean to have a pointy chin instead of a flat chin?

gloss: One of the bones, usually bearing teeth, which form the framework of the mouth.
The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.
The hair that grows over the bone ridge above the eye socket.
A thin skin membrane that covers and moves over an eye.
The soft skin on each side of the face, below the eyes; the outer surface of the sides of the oral cavity.
The front part of the neck.
example: The wild pitch bounced and hit the catcher in the throat.

gloss: The portion of the human body from the base of the neck to the top of the abdomen; the homologous area in some other animals.
example: Holonyms: torso, trunk < body

gloss: A series of bones situated at the back from the head to the pelvis of a human, or from the head to the tail of an animal, enclosing the spinal cord and providing support for the thorax and abdomen.
Any of a series of long curved bones occurring in 12 pairs in humans and other animals and extending from the spine to or toward the sternum.
The outward-projecting parts of the pelvis and top of the femur and the overlying tissue.
The upper leg of a human, between the hip and the knee.
The back of the leg below the knee.
The rear part of the foot, where it joins the leg.
The shortest and thickest digit of the hand that for humans has the most mobility and can be made to oppose (moved to touch) all of the other fingers.
The inner and somewhat concave part of the human hand or other primate hand that extends from the wrist to the bases of the fingers.
example: On the boys' palms were handfuls of sand.

gloss: A purplish mark on the skin due to leakage of blood from capillaries under the surface that have been damaged by a blow.
A small bubble between the layers of the skin that contains watery or bloody fluid and is caused by friction and pressure, burning, freezing, chemical irritation, disease, or infection.

An area of inflamed and irritated skin characterized by reddened spots that may be filled with fluid or pus. Also, preceded by a descriptive word (rare or obsolete), an illness characterized by a type of rash.
example: He came out in a rash because of an allergy.

gloss: An injury, such as a cut, stab, or tear, to a (usually external) part of the body.
A permanent mark on the skin, sometimes caused by the healing of a wound.
The act or result of spraining; lameness caused by spraining
example: a bad sprain of the wrist

gloss: A painful contraction of a muscle which cannot be controlled; (sometimes) a similar pain even without noticeable contraction.
example: He retired hurt at 31 due to a leg cramp.

gloss: The state of being swollen.
A feeling of illness or discomfort in the digestive system, usually characterized by a strong urge to vomit.
example: He got nausea after two hours of travelling on the plane.

gloss: The state of being dizzy; the sensation of instability.
A higher than normal body temperature of a person (or, generally, a mammal), usually caused by disease.
example: There has been a rise in my fever. I think I've the flu.

gloss: A sudden, often involuntary expulsion of air from the lungs through the glottis (causing a short, explosive sound), and out through the mouth.
example: Behind me, I heard a distinct, dry cough.

gloss: To expel air as a reflex induced by an irritation in the nose.
example: To avoid passing on your illness, you should sneeze into your sleeve.

gloss: A sensation felt on an area of the skin that causes a person or animal to want to scratch said area.
Causing pain or discomfort; painfully sensitive.
example: Her feet were sore from walking so far.

gloss: Rigid; hard to bend; inflexible.
Physically unable to feel, not having the power of sensation.
example: fingers numb with cold

gloss: A strip of gauze or similar material used to protect or support a wound or injury.
A viscous preparation of oils and/or fats, usually containing medication, used as a treatment or as an emollient.
example: The doctor prescribed an antibiotic ointment for the wound.

gloss: A written order from an authorized medical practitioner for provision of a medicine or other treatment, such as (ophthalmology) the specific lenses needed for a pair of glasses.
example: The surgeon had written thousands of prescriptions for pain killers without proper examinations before the police raided the clinic.

gloss: A drug that numbs the pain in the body.
example: Near-synonym: analgesia

gloss: An arrangement between people to meet; an engagement.
example: They made an appointment to meet at six.

gloss: A routine visit to the doctor, dentist, or the like.
example: The appointment was just for a checkup.

gloss: A disorder of the immune system causing adverse reactions to substances (allergens) not harmful to most and marked by the body's production of histamines and associated with atopy, anaphylaxis, and asthma; any condition of hypersensitivity to a substance.
example: My dad can't live with pets because of an allergy.

gloss: A perceived change in some function, sensation or appearance of a person that indicates a disease or disorder, such as fever, headache or rash; strictly, a symptom is felt or experienced by the patient, while a sign can be detected by an observer.
example: The doctor told that his coughing and sneezing was the symptom of standing for too long in the rain.

gloss: The part of a garment that covers the arm.
example: The sleeves on my coat are too long.

gloss: The part of an upper garment (shirt, jacket, etc.) that fits around the neck and throat, especially if sewn from a separate piece of fabric.
The end of a shirt sleeve that covers the wrist.
An utterance or sound of the voice like "hem", often indicative of hesitation or doubt, sometimes used to call attention.
A folded-back and stitched piece of fabric; especially, the stitching that joins two or more pieces of fabric.
A covering for the inside surface of something.
A zip fastener.
example: He got his T-shirt stuck in the zipper of his jacket.

gloss: A knob or disc that is passed through a loop or (buttonhole), serving as a fastener.
example: April fastened the buttons of her overcoat to keep out the wind.

gloss: A metal clasp with a hinged tongue or a spike through which a belt or strap is passed and penetrated by the tongue or spike, in order to fasten the ends of the belt together or to secure the strap to something else.
A lace used for fastening a shoe.
example: untied shoelace

gloss: The bottom of a shoe or boot.
The inside sole of a shoe or other footwear.
A bag stitched to an item of clothing, used for carrying small items.
A band of fabric encircling the waist, especially a part of a pair of pants or a skirt.
A band worn around the waist to hold clothing to one's body (usually pants), hold weapons (such as a gun or sword), or serve as a decorative piece of clothing.
example: As part of the act, the fat clown's belt broke, causing his pants to fall down.

gloss: A long, often knitted, garment worn around the neck.
A cap that fits the head closely, usually knitted from wool.
example: Enrique Iglesias is often seen wearing a beanie.

gloss: A type of sweater or jumper that fastens up the front with buttons or a zipper, usually machine- or hand-knitted from wool.
A loose shirt, usually made of a knit fleece, for athletic wear and now often used as casual apparel.
A waterproof coat to be worn in the rain; (loosely) any coat or jacket with this purpose.
A set of clothes to be worn together, now especially a man's matching jacket and trousers (also business suit or lounge suit), or a similar outfit for a woman.
example: Nick hired a navy-blue suit for the wedding.

gloss: An ornamental garment worn under a doublet.
A close-fitting, sheer or non-sheer skin-tight garment worn principally by women and girls that covers the body completely from the waist down, usually including the feet.
